items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: And like Sonny Rollins when he made that couple of trio albums there, I mean you were sitting right there for a dollar and a half.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. We were on the road and there was a group that used to appear on The Ed Sullivan Show, they were Las Vegas’s biggest act, they were called “The Goofers.” And they played rhythm & blues and they did comedy and everything. But one of the gimmicks was the sax player would swing on a trapeze. So we were playing in St. Louis and the guy had left his trapeze. So I got on it so I was fooling around and the guy says, “You think you can do that tonight?” And I said, “I’ll try.” Well that lasted about a week,…

thinking and hearing Paul Desmond, but I’d be honking, and I’d be playing all those harmonic things I heard the Claude Thornhill band play when we’re playing like some current rock tune from the day. Like “Rock Around the Clock” by Bill Haiey is nothing but a blues, right? So once we played the head and started to blow, I just blew. I was Sonny Rollins at that point you know. But I learned how to play that way and then I used to go and sit in at jam sessions and in strange towns and learn tunes and sit in with…
